chapters.title: The Real and Complex Number Systems

lectures.title: Course setup, ordered field axioms, sets, induction, relations, constructing $ℚ$
Ordered sets and fields, $\sqrt2$ irrational, upper bounds and suprema
Completeness, $ℚ$ not complete, Archimedes, density, $n$th roots, infima
Worked sup problems, extended reals, $ℝ^{k}$, Cauchy–Schwarz, cardinality
Countable sets, $ℕ×ℕ$, countable unions, Cantor's theorem
Metric spaces and examples, neighborhoods, limit/isolated/interior points
Open and closed sets, closure, complements, unions and intersections
Sup in the closure, relative openness, dense sets, open covers
Compactness: examples, compact ⇒ bounded and closed, closed ⊂ compact, nested intervals
Nested intervals, $ℝ$ uncountable, $k$-cells compact, Heine–Borel, Bolzano–Weierstrass

next.title: Finite intersection property; infinite subsets of compact sets
next.why: 2.37 was stated in L5.2 without proof. Nested compact sets have nonempty intersection.

next.title: Compactness doesn't depend on the ambient space
Perfect sets and the Cantor set
next.why: Nonempty perfect sets are uncountable; L5.2 set this up by proving $ℝ$ is uncountable with nested intervals.

next.title: Connected sets
next.why: Connected subsets of $ℝ$ are exactly the intervals.

next.title: Sequences in metric spaces, subsequences, Cauchy sequences, completeness
Monotone sequences, lim sup / lim inf, special limits
Series: tests, power series, absolute convergence, rearrangements
